title: A Flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac App Could Have Let Hackers Grab Sensitive Data
key_facts: Researchers at the Objective-See Foundation found a flaw in the macOS version of OpenAI's ChatGPT app that could have let an attacker take over the app on a victim's computer.
That would give access to all chat logs and other data stored by the app, plus connections such as browser sessions, and let the attacker make ChatGPT run commands.
The app checks digital signatures up to three layers away, but a trusted script interpreter could be made to pass an untrusted script into the main ChatGPT process by spawning itself three times.
The flaw could only be exploited by an attacker who already had malware installed on the machine; researcher Patrick Wardle's proof of concept needed about a dozen lines of code.
OpenAI acknowledged the flaw and fix in its system change log on 25 Sep 2026; spokesperson Shane Bauer said the company recognizes a need to move faster.
Wardle also found a now-patched flaw in Meta's Muse assistant and says he sent OpenAI a new report on ChatGPT's link to its new always-on Dots assistant, which OpenAI is reviewing.
